text:
maria: quick follow-up from the RFC review — I'm proposing we add an "ephemeral overlay" layer that can sit on top of shard manifests during warmup. goal is to enable hotpatches and incremental downloads without forcing a full manifest roundtrip.

kevin: can you sketch the main responsibilities? is this just a client-side cache or a new server primitive?

maria: mostly client-side + runtime helper. responsibilities: resolve logical shard -> set of physical parts (manifest + overlay), provide a verification hook (crc/sha256) during streaming, and expose a warmup plan to the prefetcher.

priya: sounds interesting. how do we handle consistency when overlay changes mid-warmup? race conditions were the painful part before.

maria: two ideas: (1) attach an "overlay epoch" to the warmup plan; if the epoch changes, abort and replan; (2) allow idempotent partial application by tracking applied byte ranges + checksums so replays are safe.

kevin: i'd prefer (2) — avoids churn for short-lived overlays. that implies we need small-range checksums in the metadata (like tiled crc). overhead ok?

priya: tiled checksums + signed manifest entries. overhead is acceptable if tile size ~64KB. gives us cheap validation for streaming and partial retries.

jonathan: what about memory layout changes? eg. we want to transpose kernels on the fly or fuse dequantization. Do we do that during warmup or lazily on first access?

maria: tradeoff: eager transform reduces tail latency for first request but increases warmup time. proposal: warmup planner returns prioritized "transform tasks" with coarse priority bands. runtime can run transforms opportunistically or block until done based on SLO.

priya: that maps nicely to existing batching and SLO plumbing. we just need the planner -> executor API to be explicit.

kevin: propose API sketch (pseudo):

```
interface OverlayResolver {
  resolve(shardId) -> {baseManifestRef, overlayRefs[], epoch, tileChecksumMap}
}

interface WarmupPlanner {
  plan(resolutionResult, budgetMs) -> [WarmupTask]
}

struct WarmupTask {
  type: [fetch|verify|transform],
  resource: url|byteRange,
  priority: int,
  idempotencyToken: string
}
```

maria: exactly. and WarmupTask should carry a small expected-hash for verification. executor must to be able to report partial progress and cancel by epoch.

jonathan: how do we expose overlays to ops? e.g., a customer wants to patch a single shard with a new quantized tile.

maria: overlay manifests are small JSON blobs we can push via control-plane API and sign. the resolver prefers overlayRefs with latest signature and epoch > base. ops will get a dry-run option to compute warmup delta.

kevin: fallback behavior if overlay missing mid-download?

priya: fallback -> fetch base tile; verify; then apply overlay if present. if overlay fails verification, rollback to base. should be explicit in planner: tasks can be conditional: "apply overlay if verified else skip".

jonathan: any perf estimate? adding tiled checksums + verification likely adds ~1-2% download CPU for hashing but cuts re-downloads and reduces soft errors. transforms cost depends on shape but can be amortized.

maria: putting numbers from our toy bench: tiled sha256 on 8GB model ~0.9s single-threaded; we can parallelize per-tile. transform (transpose + fp16 pack) on a 4GB weight file ~2.5s on a single GPU worker but can stream-convert while writing to cache.

kevin: important: ensure cache eviction plays well. if we apply overlay tiles and then evict, we must not leave dangling references. planner should mark tiles with liveness hints.

priya: agreed. add proto hint: "retainUntilEpoch=XYZ" or lease tokens returned on warmup completion.

maria: one more operational detail: when a rollback is necessary due to bad overlay, we should emit a short incident in #incidents with the shard id + overlay epoch so SRE can correlate.

deploy-bot: deploy v2.14 to infra-preview succeeded for service=weight-resolver at 2024-06-12T15:28:42Z :rocket:

jonathan: next steps: draft small RFC for the overlay resolver + warmupplanner interfaces, add tiled checksum format, and run a microbench for parallel tiled-hash cost. I'll volunteer to run perf harness.

maria: thanks — i'll draft RFC today, include the pseudo-API and a few failure-case sequences. tagging @kevin @priya for review. :thumbsup:

kevin: lgtm. please call out backward compatibility: runtime should accept manifests without tiled checksums (legacy) and default to whole-file checksum verification.

priya: also include a short migration plan for Dedicated customers — control-plane rollout of overlay signing + small client update.

maria: noted. will target RFC out by EOD and ping here when done.
